text:
Stonebeck advances toward stability as spreads hold steady

Rating: overweight

Calder & Root reads today's quiet session as confirmation, not concealment. Stonebeck enters this window with cpi_now at 2.9% and policy_rate_now at 5.00%, a pairing that continues to narrow the real-rate gap that has weighed on risk assets. Data prints in line, and a quiet session on the wire is itself informative: when the tape does not need to shout, the underlying policy path is doing its work. We view this as the mechanism by which growth and policy support resolve stress over time — not overnight, but steadily.

Grimshaw Partners argues that fragilities are compounding beneath stable marks. We do not dismiss the instinct to look under the hood, but we read the same instruments differently. hy_spread_now_bps sits at 400bps, wide enough to still be pricing caution, not complacency — a level consistent with a market demanding compensation for risk rather than ignoring it. drawdown stands at +0.0%, and one_year_return has already compounded to +11.0%, a combination that suggests resilience being rewarded rather than fragility being masked. If marks were truly hollow, we would expect drawdown to show it; instead the absence of deterioration is itself data.

The reported_vs_public_gap of -0.2% is modest and, in our structurally constructive framework, more consistent with reporting noise than with hidden stress. ytd_return of +1.1% reflects a market still building on last year's gains rather than reversing them, which fits a house view that policy support compounds gradually rather than snapping.

The risk to our own view: should hy_spread_now_bps widen meaningfully from here even as headline data continues to print in line, that divergence could signal the kind of underlying fragility Grimshaw warns of, and we would need to revisit the overweight. We think that outcome is unlikely at this stage, but it is prudent to watch the spread, not just the headline prints, before extending conviction further.
